findings.claim: The hooks layer bypasses the required hook-to-store-to-service boundary by importing and reading the graph store directly.
findings.evidence: Constraint `one-graph-layered-adapter-boundary` requires "strict component-to-hook-to-store-to-service flow", and task-2 evidence claims `components -> hooks -> platform store -> platform service -> graph/native`, but `hooks.ts` imports `useGraphStore`/`useGraphSyncStatus` from `@prometheus-ags/prometheus-entity-management` and `useTaskBoard` reads graph entities/lists/patches directly.
findings.suggested_fix: Move graph-derived selectors/state into the platform store or a store-layer selector API, have hooks consume only that store layer, and add a verifier rejection for direct graph-store imports in hooks.

findings.claim: The native capability-denial proof treats any `clearGraph` error as an authorization denial, so unrelated IPC/runtime failures can be falsely recorded as a passed trust-boundary test.
findings.evidence: Acceptance requires denied permissions to be tested and constraint `trust-boundaries-fail-closed` requires withheld destructive IPC permissions to fail closed; `proveDestructiveCommandDenied()` catches every error from `this.plugin.commands.clearGraph()` and returns `Denied as configured: ${formatError(error)}` without checking that the error is an authorization/capability denial.
findings.suggested_fix: Only return a denial proof when the error matches the expected Tauri permission-denied/not-allowed shape; otherwise rethrow or report an error so non-authorization failures cannot satisfy the denial criterion.
